newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks tumble 1.43 pct on peso panic.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks tumble 1.43 pct on peso panic.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed sharply down on Monday in response to the peso weakening substantially, traders and analysts said.
"The fall was due to the peso, but it was not representative due to the thin volume at which sales were made," said a floor trader.
The blue chip IPC index closed down 47.77 points, or 1.43 percent, at 3,287.38 points. Volume was thin at 46.8 million shares traded.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed six centavos weaker at 7.73/7.74 per dollar.

"What worried dealers were the sharp changes. If the fall had been orderly, it would have been good -- that's what dealers were asking for, particulalry foreign ones," said Rodolfo Campuzano, analyst at Invex brokerage firm in Mexico City.

Analysts also said the Bolsa was hit by expectations of hefty primary interest rate hikes at this week's central bank auction in order to prop up the peso, and news of revised petrochemical privatization plans.
"The market adjusted due to fears that the weak peso would lead to extensive primary hikes," Campuzano added.
"Information about the new privatization plans was unclear. Foreign investors are now rethinking their plans, which have been curtailed," said Roberto Galvan, analyst at the Bursametrica brokerage.
"This definitely had an impact on the market as it's a sign of things to come for further privatization."

Financial group Abaco A shares gained 11 centavos to 2.80 pesos, which traders put down to the announcement of a letter of agreement between the group and U.S.-based Principal International to form a pension fund firm (Afore).
Ceramics firm Ceramica shares ended second on the percentage losers list, but dealers said this was a single trade that did not reflect its favorable third quarter earnings posted during the session.
On the broad market, a total of 93 shares traded, losers well outnumbered gainers by 74 to 11, with eight unchanged.
Despite the day's slide, technical analysts noted that the IPC did not weaken a strong support at 3,270 points.
